newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SKANDIA SAYS NO PLANS TO BOOST POHJOLA STAKE MORE.
newsitem.headline: SKANDIA SAYS NO PLANS TO BOOST POHJOLA STAKE MORE.

text.p: Swedish insurer Skandia said on Monday it had increased its holding in Finnish insurance group Pohjola to 10.9 percent of the capital and 7.8 percent of the votes in the company.
Skandia said it had no plans to increase its holding in Pohjola further.
"At present there are no plans to further increase Skandia's holding in Pohjola," the company said in a statement.
Skandia said the increased ownership came about by Skandia exchanging 1.08 million Pohjola B-shares for Pohjola A-shares in the market.

"The change of class of shares in Pohjola ... is a move to manifest our confidence in Pohjola and our intention to remain as long term owners in the company as well as to follow more closely the on-going structural changes in Finland," it said.
Skandia's newly appointed president and chief executive, Lars-Eric Petersson, said the two companies have collaborated in the Nordic market for a number of years.
This has led to cross-ownership between them.
Pohjola's holding in Skandia amount to 10.5 percent of the shares and the votes.
